sections.content: How many people stayed in Whitehaven after gaining qualifications?

Whitehaven is a medium-sized town in the North West. Whitehaven does not have its own university.

Whitehaven has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Whitehaven ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,150 state-school pupils from Whitehaven who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 230 (20%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 400 (35%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Whitehaven to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Whitehaven's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Whitehaven in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Whitehaven move to?

Of Whitehaven's graduates, 100 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Whitehaven's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 95 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 45 of those qualified non-graduates (47%) were living fairly locally, in the Whitehaven travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Whitehaven's GCSE cohort:

  • 60 graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 33% of graduates and 28% of qualified non-graduates living in Whitehaven had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 180 graduates and 425 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Whitehaven. This is compared with the 230 graduates and 400 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 67% of the graduates had also lived in Whitehaven as GCSE pupils, while 33% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Whitehaven in 2018 to 2019, 72% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 28% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
